name: Pelican
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four guys from Chicago kept metal's riffs, left the singer at home, and wrote songs so long they could only fit five of them into a 75-minute set.

eras.title: Out of the grind
eras.text: Pelican grew out of Chicago's heavy underground: Trevor de Brauw and drummer Larry Herweg had played in the experimental grind band Tusk. With a second guitarist, Laurent Schroeder-Lebec, and Larry's brother Bryan on bass, they dropped vocals entirely and signed to Hydra Head, the label run by Isis's Aaron Turner.

years.h: Pelican forms in Chicago: two guitars, two Herwegs, no singer
years.p: Trevor de Brauw and Laurent Schroeder-Lebec on guitars and brothers Bryan and Larry Herweg on bass and drums start Pelican as an instrumental band.
years.xp: De Brauw and Larry Herweg came from Tusk, an experimental grind project with their friend Jody Minnoch. Pelican's own label bio lists influences as far apart as post-hardcore, space rock, emo and metal.

years.h: Pelican EP on Hydra Head, recorded by Sanford Parker
years.p: Pelican's first release, a self-titled EP, comes out on Hydra Head. Chicago engineer [[Sanford Parker|f52da716-09e2-49d5-b385-227d03d9b7cf]] recorded it; he would record the band again 22 years later.

years.h: Australasia: rushed, broke, in a studio under construction
years.p: Pelican's debut album was made fast at Chicago's Volume Studios with Sanford Parker. Trevor de Brauw blamed budget limits for the rush, and the studio was being rebuilt around them.
years.xp: Six songs, 50 minutes: four of them run past eight minutes. Drought later turned up in the 2009 war film The Messenger.

eras.title: Heavy without a word
eras.text: Pelican toured hard in Europe and the US and became a flagship of what writers were starting to call post-metal. The records got more melodic and more ambitious, recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio, and the metal press took them seriously even as some early fans missed the sludge.

years.h: Pelican on the road in Spain at Sant Feliu Fest
years.p: A year after Australasia, Pelican is already playing European festivals, including Sant Feliu Fest in Catalonia.

q: The title is meant to confuse people.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw
years.h: The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw
years.p: Recorded in February 2005 at Electrical Audio, Pelican's second album adds acoustic guitar and nature themes like Aurora Borealis. Decibel named it the best album of 2005.
years.xp: The album moved away from Australasia's crush toward layered melody, and some longtime fans didn't love it. Critics reached for doom metal, post-rock and [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]] to describe it. It reached No. 44 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
play: The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw

years.h: Pelican records City of Echoes at Electrical Audio
years.p: Pelican cuts its third album at Electrical Audio in Chicago with producer Andrew Schneider.
Laurent Schroeder-Lebec called City of Echoes Pelican's pop album: shorter songs, bigger melodies. Their old songs were so long they could only play five in a 75-minute set.
years.xp: Trevor de Brauw said the title was about globalization: travel all over and every city starts to look the same. The band said it wasn't all gloom, since touring was how they met audiences worldwide. The album hit No. 9 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 40 on Independent Albums.

eras.title: Overextended
eras.text: Pelican left Hydra Head for Southern Lord, got its biggest recording budget and first sang on a record. It also ran itself down: too much touring, family illness, and a founding guitarist who stopped coming on the road.

years.h: Pelican leaves Hydra Head for Southern Lord
years.p: Pelican moves from Hydra Head to Southern Lord, the label run by [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]]'s [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]].

years.h: Ephemeral EP and a tour with Wolves in the Throne Room
years.p: Pelican's first Southern Lord release is a short EP, supported by a tour with [[Wolves in the Throne Room|e9452446-7702-4853-96ce-5dfe6748d3fb]]. The song Ephemeral later played over the end credits of Dead Space 3.

years.src: Wikipedia: What We All Come to Need · Wikipedia: Pelican
years.h: What We All Come to Need: Pelican finally has a singer
years.p: Recorded in three weeks in Washington State with Chris Common, the album brings in [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] and [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]]. [[Allen Epley|7b7fb455-c63c-49ca-82f4-b9c8da828bf0]] of [[Shiner|85e4c862-bafe-48a2-a7af-b87cc3d8a7f3]] sings closer Final Breath, Pelican's first vocal on a studio album.
years.xp: Chicago's Kuma's Corner put a Pelican Burger on the menu to celebrate the release. Behind the scenes, the band was worn out: Trevor de Brauw's mother was ill, and he said they had way overextended themselves by the end of the year.
play: What We All Come to Need

years.h: Pelican tours Europe: Roadburn and Dunk festivals
years.p: Pelican's spring 2012 European tour takes in Roadburn in the Netherlands and Dunk in Belgium, with Bo Ningen, Tacoma Narrows Bridge Disaster and Tombs in support.

years.h: Laurent Schroeder-Lebec leaves; Dallas Thomas joins
years.p: Founding guitarist Laurent Schroeder-Lebec quits after the Ataraxia/Taraxis EP, saying his heart wasn't fully in it. He hadn't toured in two years; Dallas Thomas of The Swan King had been filling in.
years.xp: Thomas had played live but not written. Now he became a full member and a songwriter, and the next record would be the first without a founder.

eras.title: Darker, and grieving
eras.text: With Dallas Thomas on guitar, Pelican got angrier. Then the death of an old friend from the Tusk days sent Trevor de Brauw and Larry Herweg back to their grind roots, and produced the band's first charting album.

years.h: Forever Becoming, the first album without a founder
years.p: Recorded at Electrical Audio with Chris Common, Forever Becoming was darker, depressive and angry, Trevor de Brauw said, because of the line-up uncertainty. It hit No. 21 on Billboard's Top Hard Rock Albums.
Pelican's sixth album is shaped by the death of Jody Minnoch, Trevor de Brauw and Larry Herweg's bandmate in Tusk, who died suddenly of an undiagnosed heart condition. The title came from his notes.
years.xp: De Brauw and Herweg went back to Tusk's grind for fuel, and de Brauw called the chord voicings discordant and menacing, more negative than Pelican had sounded. Recorded at Electrical Audio and Decade Music Studios, it reached No. 37 on the UK Rock & Metal chart, Pelican's first chart album in Britain. NPR called Midnight and Mescaline a barrage of heavy riffs.

years.h: Nighttime Stories tour with Cloakroom and Slow Crush
years.p: Pelican tours North America, the UK and Europe behind Nighttime Stories, with [[Cloakroom|d419f6da-298a-40ea-ba0c-1757edd218b7]] and Slow Crush among the support.

eras.title: Laurent comes home
eras.text: Dallas Thomas's exit opened the door for Laurent Schroeder-Lebec to return, restoring the original four. The early catalog got a second life, and a new label, Run for Cover Records, put out Pelican's first album in six years.

years.h: Dallas Thomas leaves; Laurent Schroeder-Lebec returns
years.p: With Dallas Thomas gone, founding guitarist Laurent Schroeder-Lebec rejoins Pelican for live shows, and the original line-up is back.

years.h: Pelican's first three albums get deluxe remasters
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Australasia, The Fire in Our Throats Will Beckon the Thaw and City of Echoes were given deluxe remasters through Thrill Jockey.

years.h: Cascading Crescent: Pelican's first new song in six years
years.p: Pelican previews its seventh album with Cascading Crescent, followed by Indelible, Pining For Ever and Gulch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Flickering Resonance · Run For Cover Records
years.h: Flickering Resonance: the original four, and Sanford Parker again
years.p: Laurent Schroeder-Lebec's first Pelican album since 2009 is recorded at Chicago's Narwhal Studios by [[Sanford Parker|f52da716-09e2-49d5-b385-227d03d9b7cf]], who made their first EP. Pelican tours it with [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]].
years.xp: Run for Cover describes a more collaborative record, with all four sharing decisions. Christian Degn's cover centers on a flame, about how the smallest flames can bring the biggest changes.
